subject: Commitment banding and measurement gates for hosted response guarantees
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@finsight.ai>

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted SLO framing for procurement assessment

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the host routing and autoscale example was helpful. As we move to procurement, our legal and infra teams need a clear definition of the latency commitments and how you measure them. Two specific asks:  

1) The numerical targets you expect to commit to (p50 and p95) for the hosted API under our expected load profile (~12k reqs/min).
2) The measurement windowing and carveouts you use for transient bursts, maintenance, and regional failovers.

We want to avoid ambiguous wording in the SOW. Can you send a one-page framing we can include in the SOW + a short evidence checklist we can use for audits?

Attached: our internal procurement checklist (FYI).

Cheers,
Megan Liu
Head of Platform Operations
FinSight Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO framing for procurement assessment

Megan — thanks for the clear asks. I drafted a concise framing below you can drop into the SOW; I also attached two artifacts (SLO evidence templates and a CSV with the proposed bands). High level proposal:  

- Commitment bands (example workload): p50 = 55ms, p95 = 360ms for "standard" tier traffic.  
- Measurement gates: 24h sliding epoch evaluated at hourly rollups; daily reporting cadence for contractual compliance. 
- Transient carveouts: automatic exclusion for scheduled maintenance windows and for burst events that match our burst definition (see below).

Burst definition (proposed): a burst is a contiguous 10-minute window where 95th percentile per-minute request rate exceeds 5x baseline and is accompanied by backend capacity rebalancing (autoscale events). If a burst qualifies, token-level measurements in that 10-minute window are tagged and excluded from the daily contractual percentile calculation; evidence bundle required.

Evidence bundle (what we will provide when a carveout is invoked):
- Aggregated request-rate timeline (1m granularity)
- Autoscaler event logs and capacity change timestamps
- Request/response histograms (500ms buckets) and request ids for sampling
- Relevant alerting/tracing spans (trace ids)

If that sounds reasonable I can loop Ben to confirm the measurement signals we will include in the evidence package and Lauren to confirm the SOW wording.

Next steps: if you want to tighten p95 for procurement, tell me the acceptable threshold and we can model credits.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Omar Patel <omar.patel@finsight.ai>

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO framing for procurement assessment

Karthik/Team,

Appreciate the quick draft. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and procurement leads:  

- The p95 360ms number is fair on paper, but our lawyers want a clause for sustained regional degradation (we operate primarily in us-west and need confidence in regional fallbacks). How does Redwood account for regional failover periods in the measurement gates?
- We also need to understand the credit model if p95 breaches persist more than 3 consecutive days. Is there an automated measurement and remediation path, or will this be decisions on a case-by-case basis?

On tightening: we could accept 360ms if there is a tiered credit schedule (small % credits per day breached, escalating after day 3) and a clear regional failover carveout.

Can Ben or Lauren propose the operational wording you would accept?

Thanks,
Omar
Director, Infrastructure
FinSight Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Omar Patel <omar.patel@finsight.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO framing for procurement assessment

Omar — quick technical clarifications and an operational proposal from infra:  

1) Regional failovers: measurement is per-region by default. If a routed request is served from an alternate region due to a documented outage (failover routing policy engaged), those requests can be marked in the evidence bundle and excluded from the offending region's daily contractual percentile calculation provided the failover meets these conditions:  
   - Failover initiated by automated routing policy OR documented region-level incident (PagerDuty incident id required)
   - Customer traffic volume shifted >30% for >15 minutes or routing TTL changes logged

2) Sustained breaches: propose an automated daily assessment with a tiered credit schedule:  
   - Day 1 breach: remediation SLA triggered; 2% credit on affected day's invoice if p95 > committed by >25%
   - Day 2 breach: 5% credit if not remediated within 24h after remediation SLA start
   - Day 3+: escalated executive review and 10% credit/day until mitigation plan accepted

3) Measurement gating: to avoid noisy short-term fluctuations we will use a 24h sliding epoch with hourly sub-aggregation. Contractual evaluation runs at midnight UTC for the prior 24h window. Carveouts (scheduled maintenance, verified failover, qualifying burst) require an evidence bundle and a formal request inside 72h to be processed for exclusion.

I'll attach the CSV with the band examples and the template for evidence we referenced. If that's acceptable we can convert this language into SOW text and route to legal.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Reliability Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is converging nicely. Summary and proposed SOW snippet below you can copy/paste into your doc:  

--- SOW SNIPPET (proposed) ---
Redwood Inference will provide hosted API response time commitments for the agreed contract scope as follows:
- Commitment band: p50 = 55ms; p95 = 360ms for "standard" tier traffic, measured per-region.
- Measurement window: 24-hour sliding epoch evaluated hourly; official contractual evaluation runs daily at 00:00 UTC for the prior 24-hour window.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified), qualifying bursts (10-minute window where request-rate 95p >5x baseline and autoscaler activity observed), and documented region-level failovers (PagerDuty incident id + routing logs) may be excluded from contractual calculations. Customer must submit an evidence bundle within 72 hours for exclusion processing.
- Credits: tiered credit schedule applies for sustained p95 breaches (Day 1: 2%, Day 2: 5%, Day 3+: 10% per day) with executive engagement after Day 3.

---

Action items:
- FinSight: confirm acceptance of the p95 360ms band or propose alternative threshold by EOD Mon 9/13.
- Redwood: we will prepare a one-page evidence checklist + SOW paragraph and circulate for legal review (link to draft contract above).

I attached the evidence template and the commitment chart. If you confirm the p95 band we'll draft the formal addendum and route to DocuSign.

Best,
